ws.name: WS1 Minimap and the side-box channel (map_bp first)
ws.brief:
ITEMS: O1 (F46/F56/F70 W1: map_bp 3.9 ms against 1, and the bundle under 5 at 40), O2 for elytra_bp/saga_bp/calendar_bp, O5 (the actual 100-player Map and Saga quest windows, F57), O10's map rebuild wave every 200 ticks, and O6's native 100-player hud_state proof (it rides in the same 100-player runs). Do NOT edit tools/name-labels-shared.js or tools/tether-shared.js: WS3 owns them, even though saga has copies. Don't touch the build/stash/stats (group 2) or living-towns (group 5) code.

MEASURED COST (base master, steady window at 40 / 100 players, 67-context soak): map_bp 3.907 / 4.028 ms (10 players: 3.091; one-context bundle at 10: 2.29 of 4.28). Callbacks: runInterval(1) redraw main.js:1290-1356 = 1.984 / 2.072 ms, max 300 ms; runInterval(1) scanner main.js:700-809 = 1.241 / 1.268; runInterval(1) passes main.js:1421-1455 = 0.561 / 0.563; side.js:358-375 sweep = 0.098. setTitle is 1.10/tick, and each draw also sends 2 realm:side events (compass and radar parts, side-shared.js:277) with the 1.3 KB radar text. That makes map the source of almost all of the ~2.18 realm: events/tick. Each event wakes every pack's listener: script-events.js:80 costs 1.36 ms/tick summed over 66 packs at 40. The six other side consumers pay the most because each JSON.parses the radar message: calendar 0.102, saga 0.097, hud 0.092, elytra 0.090, maps 0.083, mobhp 0.075 ms for script events alone. Other costs: saga main.js:70-121 loop 0.081 / 0.143 (r1 line numbers; base :121); elytra main.js:576-695 per-tick loop 0.100 / 0.145; hud main.js:119-144 0.058 / 0.095. Totals at 40: elytra 0.253, saga 0.225, hud 0.186, calendar 0.143, maps 0.137, mobhp 0.108.

APPROACHES:
(1) The side protocol, in side-shared.js and synced: stop broadcasting the minimap's per-draw text.
- Option A, a compositor claim: the pack that draws most for a player (map, while it has a view) sends realm:side_comp {player, from, until}. While that claim is live, the other packs still send their own small slot changes, but they don't redraw that player. The compositor never broadcasts its own compass or radar text. When the claim ends or expires (about 60 ticks), the old behavior resumes, so the packs stay independent and every one still works alone.
- Minimum fallback if A is rejected: one realm:side event carrying both parts.
- In every consumer, keep the raw message per (player, from) and JSON.parse it only when drawing.
- Target: realm: events about 2.2/tick to under 0.5/tick. That should cut roughly 1 ms/tick of listener wakes across all 67 packs at 40 and bring each side consumer's script-event cost to about 0.02.
- Keep the realm: id rule. A separate namespace for side traffic would need an owner answer, because CLAUDE.md requires realm: ids.
(2) The map redraw at :1290-1356.
- Read the split first: turnCheckMs, radarMs and the costMs send share, via realm:map_debug.
- Read each player's pose (location, getRotation, dimension) once per tick in a snapshot shared by the scanner, the redraw and the passes; extend playersNow() at :691.
- Make radarOf (:928) reuse terrain rows and pictures for players at the same rounded pose, heading step and store version. The soak's groups of 5 stand together.
- Skip setTitle and the side send when the composed text hasn't changed.
- Spread REFRESH keep-alive resends by player id slot (O5's concern: keep-alives using up drawBudget at 100).
- Because the work is budget-bound (draw 1, rebuild 0.4, pass 0.5, scan 1 ms/tick at budgetLevel normal, main.js:655, 1275-1276, 1385), cheaper units alone just buy more frames. Add a demand cap: each player is drawn only when something visible changed, at most once per N ticks, so the saved time actually lowers ms/tick. Don't change TURN_MIN, MOVE_MIN or the budgetLevel meanings without a measurement and a note for the owner: O15's real-client check of low, normal and high is still pending.
(3) The scanner at :700-809.
- Don't re-plan stationary players (planFor :812 reads location and terrain every PLAN_EVERY).
- Dedupe columns across viewers of the same store.
- Stop spending the saved-up scanBudget (max 30 ms) when every plan is complete.
- Check whether stable 2.1.0 has a cheaper top-block read than per-column readers; confirm in the typings.
(4) The passes at :1421-1455: reuse the shared pose snapshot; skip players with compass and radar both off; lengthen INTERVAL for players who haven't moved; npcsNear (:455) should use event-fed positions rather than entity queries where possible.
(5) O10: stagger the 200-tick terrain rebuild (:915) per player so the rebuilds don't align. Report p95 and max tick before and after.
(6) Saga: send per-player sendSeals, sendFlags, sendProgress and sendWanderState (main.js:80-86) only when the payload changed, and batch players into multi-part messages under 2048 chars. For idle players, the story tracker should skip unchanged draws (O5).
(7) Elytra: poll isGliding every 10 ticks into a gliders set; the per-2-tick spark loop (:663-695) then visits only gliders.
(8) Hud: send realm:hud_state only when the seeing set changes; it already uses parts after O6.
- Bump versions, run sync-side, sync-diag, help-catalog only if docs change, and npm run check.
TARGETS at 40: map_bp <= 1 ms (or report exactly how far measurements allow, with the remaining split); elytra, saga, calendar <= 0.15; hud, maps, mobhp no worse. Every map_bp functional scenario must still pass, plus saga-quest-box, saga-quest-wrap and maps-warmth-steady. Map ones: map, map-turn, map-flight, map-empty-panels, map-others-range, map-places, map-reset, map-water-structures, rook-map-race.

  node tools/test-bds/run.mjs --quiet --no-relay --profile --profile-json <out>/ws1-<tree>-<N>.json --only map_bp,hud_bp,saga_bp,elytra_bp,calendar_bp,maps_bp,mobhp_bp,afk_bp --scenario tools/test-bds/examples/perf-soak.js --arg players=<10|40> --arg seconds=120 --timeout 3000

items.summary:
The side-box traffic is fixed. map_bp is now the side boxes' compositor. It sends realm:side_comp claims: one per new player, then one renewal every 40 ticks for 100, with at most 60 ids per message. It never broadcasts its 1.3 KB compass or radar. While a claim is live, the other packs still send their own small slot changes but don't draw that player; map draws their slots inside its own title. When a claim ends or runs out, each pack draws again on its own. Other packs' messages are parsed only when a copy draws that player, and each copy caches its composed segments and subtitle.

Map-side cuts:
- A still player's 30-tick refresh redraws the cached title without rebuilding the strip or radar.
- A pass marks a view dirty only when its markers moved 0.25 block or more, or its second line or settings changed.
- A jump keeps a roofed viewer's cave layer, so the scanner no longer re-reads a whole new layer store.
- The 200-tick rebuild is staggered per player (O10), and refresh-due players are always checked (O5).

items.summary: durability_bp 1.2.10 -> 1.2.11. Before, every player's main hand and off hand were read every 10 ticks, and their armor every 40. Now held items are checked at the next check after a break, a block or entity interaction, an item use (use, release, complete, stop-use-on), a hit on an entity or block, a hotbar change or an inventory change. Armor is checked after the player is hurt, spawns, or moves a wearable item into or out of the inventory. A worn elytra is checked every 4th check, because gliding fires no event. Every slot of every player is also checked once every 10 checks (5 s), spread by a hash of the player id. Turning warnings back on checks at once. Those items wear with no event: a shield that fully blocks a hit causes no hurt, and a brush wears when brushing ends. items.summary: Added a shared spreader, tools/spread-shared.js. node tools/sync-spread.mjs copies it into each pack as scripts/spread.js, and its --check runs in npm run check. Every player is still visited once every N ticks, but a fair share of them runs on each of K runs, and each player keeps their slot by player id. Moved every per-player sweep in the 9 packs onto it. Atlas: 40 ticks in 10 shares. Quests, Milestones, Titles, Guilds, AFK: 20 ticks in 10 shares. Journal: 80 ticks in 10 shares. Milestones check: checkSeconds shares. Dolphin: 5 ticks in 5 shares. Milestones looks up each Stats objective once per check run and skips milestones already at their top tier. Titles reads position and dimension once, and reads time of day and weather once a round. AFK skips the movement read once a player has turned, and its night-skip count runs once a round. Journal reads the dimension id once per look and the world spawn once a round. Nicknames: the every-player-every-10-ticks refreshAll is gone. AFK and Titles now send realm:nametag {player, from}, Nicknames fixes that player's tag at once, and a 5-second spread sweep catches the rest. PACKS.md now says that Deck of Many Things' rainbow or false-title name tag is put right only by that 5-second check (review fix 54655b7). items.summary: gauntlet.js keeps a world-side mark for each stored record (expedition:cart_marks, {tag: 0 = put down | 1 = seen}), so knowing that the carts were there no longer depends on the player. From the put-down tick, the world looks for the carts at once and then every tick for 40 ticks. While that window is open it listens to beforeEvents.entityRemove (subscribed only during the window), and the entityLoad hook marks carts that load later. cartsOf treats a seen mark as seen, and look() no longer hands back a cart that was broken during its recheck. Reviewer fix (58b60ce): the cap is now 800 (about 23K chars, under the 32767 limit). Over the cap, the oldest 0 marks are dropped first, and a 1 mark only when no 0 mark is left; the mark just made is never dropped. cartsOf now copies a seen mark onto the record as seen when the hand-over runs again, so the mark no longer has to last after that. expedition_bp 2.4.12 -> 2.4.13 (still unreleased, so not bumped again; diag in sync). Over the cap, the oldest 0 marks are dropped first, a 1 mark only when no 0 mark is left, and the mark just made is never dropped. Reason: dropping a 0 mark only brings back the old behavior for carts that never appeared, while dropping a 1 mark can copy items.

Finding 2: MARKS_MAX raised from 200 to 800. Reason: a tag is about 30 chars, so 800 marks stay near 23K chars, under the 32767 dynamic-property limit, and dead seen marks from players who never return need four times more churn to matter.

Finding 2: cartsOf copies a seen mark onto the record as seen when the hand-over runs again. Reason: from then on the record no longer depends on the mark. A stash record lives on the player, so it cannot learn this while they are away; that is why the eviction order is the main fix.
